# zod Advisory Review — 2026-10-26

[GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5) (high): zod can
exhaust memory while validating oversized constrained collections. Every release before
**4.6.6** is affected and no 3.x release carries the fix, so the production scan in
`.github/workflows/security.yml` (`npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`) failed on the
locked zod 3.25.76.

## Where zod runs

Only in the browser. The forms validate what a person types — sign-in, create account, password
recovery, a new password, the profile name and the change-password form — and the response
interceptor compares the bodies of five GET endpoints with the client's contract
(`frontend/src/lib/api-contract.ts`). None of the .NET services use it. The collections it checks
come from the visitor's own input or from Planora's own API, so the reachable effect is a tab
exhausting its own memory; the update is made because the fixed release exists and the
production scan is a blocking gate.

## Change

| Package | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `zod` | 3.25.76 (`^3.24.1`) | **4.6.7** (`^4.6.7`) | first fixed major; npm audit resolves to 4.6.7 |
| `@hookform/resolvers` | 3.10.0 (`^3.9.1`) | **5.9.2** (`^5.9.2`) | the 3.x `zodResolver` reads only zod 3 schemas |

The 5.x resolver lists `ajv ^8.12.0` among its optional peers, so npm places ajv 8.20.0 at the
top of the tree (ESLint keeps its own ajv 6). The application never imports it.

What zod 4 changes for Planora:

- Form messages and their order are the same: each check carries its own message, and the auth
  page tests pin them all — three were added for this change (a malformed address on sign-in,
  create account and recovery; an empty confirmation on create account and on a new password).
- A failed object check still runs the password-confirmation refinement, as zod 3 did for string
  fields, and `zodResolver` still shows the first message per field.
- An `invalid_type` issue no longer says what it received. The contract report reads the type
  from the response body instead, so it still says `(expected string, got number)`.
